verdictNote: Freeze and protocol are intact and the instrument is reliable on its validation and on everything reproduced here. The holdout is invalid because registered critical coverage is missing: CARRIER_HOLD has 0 units (PREREG-2 Δ9), no H1 race week holds only the race touch, an optional shakeout and the race (PREREG-6 Δ18, Δ29), no re-entry week has an optional session left undone (PREREG-6 Δ5), no case delivers a whole plan week executed in full in both sports between two breaks (PREREG-5 Δ3), and the clinical-flag break with clearance (PREREG-3 Δ6) and the directly answered UNREPORTED_TRAINING question (PREREG-2 Δ9) each have one evaluable case where two are required, the first after losing R7D-F22 to a CORPUS_ERROR. Each clause names INVALID_HOLDOUT as its consequence. The invalidity hides one confirmed blocker on a valid case: QRE-P4-F01 (P03(d), R7D-F13), a structural GENERALIZATION_BLOCKER, pre-existing since R7C-FREEZE-4. So the valid evidence already excludes READY, independently of the invalidity. The other three automated FAIL units are HARNESS_GAP and return as not evaluated, never as PASS.

automatedFailures.unit: week 8, mode EASY, 13 unreported runs (w3-run-d5 … w7-run-d5) in the window 2026-12-12..2027-01-10
automatedFailures.mechanism: s1 is a WEEKLY_REVIEW at w7 d6 20:00 with no observation; the record is empty (nothing reported since the start). Gates read the reviewed week as MISSED (HOLD, 'repeat the dose'); with no completed run in the 30-day window the reviewed entry (15 min) becomes the ceiling, and the plan is trimmed from EASY 20/EASY 20/LONG 15 to 15/15/15 (week 8, CONSOLIDATION) and from 20/20/25 to 15/15/20 (week 9), VALID, with no question. runGapInForce reads only the decision's own week, which has no run left on Sunday evening, and the composition's dependence test did not fire for this week.

automatedFailures.unit: week 5, mode EASY, 8 unreported runs before week 5
automatedFailures.mechanism: s3 is the week-5 review on its last day (2027-03-07 20:00). The only week-5 run on or after the decision date is w5-run-d6 (LONG 65), which s3's own observations report completed (65 min). The decision plans from week 6 (REESTABLISH fromWeek 6), whose window holds the week-5 completed runs (41, 40, 65), and that unit passes. The harness counts a session the same decision records as executed as if it were a run dose still planned.

The variant replaces s2, which is both the answer and the week-4 WEEKLY_REVIEW, with a pain EXERCISE_SUBSTITUTION, and compares at s3, the week-5 review a week later. So the carried run (1) never reviews week 4, (2) spends week 5 under the pre-answer plan (EASY 40/35/LONG 60; a clinical route adopts nothing) while the direct run had week 5 re-planned to 35/35/46, and (3) receives different facts at s3, because s3's bulk asPrescribed reports expand against each run's plan in force (carried: 40/35/60 run minutes, 51/50 strength minutes; direct: 35/35/46, 33/31). The plans then differ (w5d6 LONG 60 vs 46, both already executed; w6 LONG 55 vs 51; dead-bug 2 vs 3 sets). The recorded answer rows (weeks 3–4) are identical in both ledgers. With the first eligible decision placed before any session elapses (the harness's own probe form, w4 d6 23:30), carried and direct are identical in plan, validity and question.

automatedFailures.unit: w0-run-d0, w0-run-d2, w0-run-d5 EASY 15 against ceiling 5; w1-run-d5 EASY 20 against ceiling 5; reference INTAKE_LONGEST 0 min on 2026-11-28
automatedFailures.mechanism: The intake states recent.longestRunMinutes 0 after a 14-week stop. The harness pushes it as an INTAKE_LONGEST reference of 0 minutes (Number.isFinite(0)), so the ceiling is 0 + 5 = 5, below the policy's minimumSessionMinutes (15): no run could ever pass. The policy reads no completed run in the window as 'the reviewed entry (return.entryRunMinutes = 15) is the ceiling'. With the field absent, the runtime output is byte-identical and the harness gives NOT_EVALUABLE (NO_RUN_REFERENCE_IN_WINDOW) for the same two weeks.

propertiesAndRelations.questionsWithNoExit: No ASK without an exit the interface allows was found. R7D-F15 (s1, s2) and R7D-F30 (s2 to s4) ask 'the interruption reason is unclear' (missingInputs interruption.reasonCategory) because their free text holds a word the R6 reason screen treats as ambiguous ('back next Wednesday'; 'two-day off-site'). Witnesses show the exit: re-sending the break by name with plain text, or with the category and no free text, applies it (F15 s2 MODIFY; F30 s2 to s4 MODIFY, MODIFY, KEEP). In the holdout these questions were left unanswered by the timeline (QRE-P4-O01). The one state without a true exit is the disclosed F08 boundary (R7D-F23; QRE-P4-R02). R7D-F21's UNREPORTED_TRAINING question (s2) is left by evidence: week 5's completed runs make the week-6 dose independent of the unknown window.

evidence.impact: the coach plans entry-level doses (15 min) VALID after seven unknown weeks without asking: the zero reading. Doses fall, never rise, so it is not a SAFETY_BLOCKER (P03 class: SAFETY only if the dose rises); the athlete who trained gets a silent 20 % to 33 % cut (EASY 20 to 15, LONG 25 or 30 to 20) and no chance to report.

p03 checks the current week's capped runs with date >= asOfLocal; for a review on the week's last day this includes w5-run-d6 (2027-03-07), which s3's own observations report completed (65 min). The decision's re-plan starts at week 6 (REESTABLISH fromWeek 6), and the week-6 unit, whose window holds the week-5 completed runs, passes.
